cards.explanation: The answer is cave. David takes refuge in the cave of Adullam after he leaves Gath. A cave is a solid hiding spot, friends, though I bet the echo makes every whisper sound like an announcement. This is where David's story picks up.

The answer is that they go down to him there. His brothers and the rest of his father's household hear about it, and they go down to David at the cave. The text doesn't say why they came, so I won't tell you. I think it had to mean something that family showed up at a cave. Nobody mails a card to a cave, friends, so showing up in person says a lot.

The answer is leader. Everyone who was distressed or indebted or discontented rallied around David, and he became their leader. About four hundred men were with him. David went to a cave for refuge and ended up with a crowd, friends, which is the least quiet refuge I've ever heard of.

The answer is God. David says to the king of Moab at Mizpeh of Moab, “Please let my father and mother stay with you until I learn what God will do for me.” David asks for a safe place for his parents, and he says out loud that he's waiting to learn what God will do for him. I like that he put it in those words.

The answer is that Gad tells David to leave the stronghold and go into Judah. Gad, a prophet, says, “Do not stay in the stronghold. Depart and go into the land of Judah.” David leaves and goes to the forest of Hereth. Gad says go, friends, and the very next thing the text says is that David left.

The answer is that Saul accuses them of conspiring against him. Saul says to his servants, the men of Benjamin, “Is that why all of you have conspired against me?” He has his spear in hand, and he asks whether David is giving them fields and vineyards and making them commanders. Conspiring is the charge, friends, and it comes out of Saul's own mouth.

The answer is that Doeg saw David come to Ahimelech at Nob. Doeg the Edomite says, “I saw the son of Jesse come to Ahimelech son of Ahitub at Nob.” Ahimelech is the priest at Nob, and Doeg is with Saul's servants when he says it. I think it got very quiet right after that.

The answer is False. Doeg tells Saul that Ahimelech inquired of the LORD for David and gave him provisions. He also says Ahimelech gave David the sword of Goliath the Philistine, the giant David defeated (1 Samuel 17:50). David didn't leave with nothing, friends. Doeg's report listed what he got.

The answer is that David could rise up against Saul. Saul says Ahimelech did it all “…so that he could rise up against me to lie in wait, as he is doing today.” Bread, a sword and inquiring of God are the three things on his list. That's Saul's accusation in Saul's words, friends. Ahimelech has an answer for it.

The answer is True. Ahimelech says it right to Saul's face: “Who among all your servants is as faithful as David, the king’s son-in-law, the captain of your bodyguard and honored in your house?” Saul is the king, and this is a priest talking to him. That's some nerve, friends, talking like that to the king. Ahimelech says it anyway.

The answer is nothing. Ahimelech says, “…your servant knew nothing of this whole affair…” He asks the king not to accuse him or anyone in his father's household. He's pleading, friends, and he says he himself knew nothing. It's the plainest way to say it.

The answer is False, and it's a heavy one. Saul answers Ahimelech, “You will surely die, Ahimelech, you and all your father’s house!” He doesn't spare him after hearing the plea. I think this is a hard verse to sit with, friends.

The answer is False. Saul orders the guards at his side to kill the priests of the LORD, but “…the king’s servants would not lift a hand to strike the priests of the LORD.” They refuse, friends. The order then goes to someone else.

The answer is David. Abiathar, one of the sons of Ahimelech, escapes and flees to David. He's the one who gets away from Nob. Then Abiathar tells David that Saul has killed the priests of the LORD. He's carrying very hard news, friends.

The answer is that Doeg was there and was sure to tell Saul. David says, “I knew that Doeg the Edomite was there that day, and that he was sure to tell Saul.” Doeg is the man who spoke up in front of Saul. David says it to Abiathar, the priest's son who just brought him the news. This is a heavy part of the story, friends.

The answer is responsible. David says to Abiathar, the son who escaped, “I myself am responsible for the lives of everyone in your father’s house.” David doesn't pass the blame to anybody, friends. He takes it on himself, and he says it plainly.

The answer is that David tells Abiathar to stay with him and not be afraid. David says, “Stay with me; do not be afraid, for he who seeks your life is seeking mine as well. You will be safe with me.” The one after Abiathar is the same one after David, so David puts them side by side. For a man who just lost his family, friends, I bet that offer meant a lot.
